title: Microtasks versus macrotasks (event loop ordering)
hook: Promise.then callbacks are microtasks. setTimeout callbacks are macrotasks. The engine drains all microtasks before the next macrotask — that ordering explains half of senior JavaScript interview output questions and subtle race bugs in production.

blocks.text: **Microtasks** (jobs) include Promise reactions (`then`, `catch`, `finally`), `queueMicrotask`, and `MutationObserver` callbacks in browsers. **Macrotasks** (tasks) include `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, I/O callbacks in Node.js, and UI events. After synchronous JavaScript finishes, the engine runs **every** queued microtask — including microtasks scheduled by other microtasks — before dequeuing the next macrotask. `async/await` desugars to Promise microtasks, so `await` continuations follow the same rules.

entries.plainDefinition: High-priority queue drained to completion after each stack turn.
entries.example: Promise.resolve().then(fn) enqueues fn as a microtask.

entries.plainDefinition: Lower-priority queue processed one task per event loop iteration (after microtasks).
Syntax that pauses an async function and resumes via a Promise microtask when the awaited value settles.
entries.example: After await fetch(), the continuation is a microtask.

blocks.text: Reddit and LeetCode discussions rank **event loop ordering** among the top FAANG JavaScript questions. Misordering causes bugs: you log state before a Promise callback mutates it, you assume `setTimeout(0)` runs before `then`, or you starve macrotasks by chaining infinite microtasks. In React 18, automatic batching still respects microtasks — understanding queues helps debug state updates after `await`.

blocks.title: Node.js extra: process.nextTick
blocks.body: In Node.js, `process.nextTick` runs before other microtasks — even before Promise reactions. Treat it as an ultra-high-priority queue that can starve I/O if abused.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Sync first
items.body: All synchronous code in the current call stack runs to completion.

items.title: Microtasks until empty
items.body: Run microtasks FIFO; if a microtask queues another, run that too — before any macrotask.

items.title: One macrotask
items.body: Dequeue and run exactly one macrotask.

items.title: Repeat
items.body: Return to microtask draining for the next turn.

snippet.label: Nested microtasks vs macrotask
snippet.explanation: Nested Promise.then (promise 2) is still a microtask scheduled during microtask draining — it runs before the timer macrotask.

snippet.label: async/await ordering
snippet.explanation: demo runs until await, then the caller continues synchronously. The async function body resumes as a microtask after the current sync code finishes.

snippet.label: Node.js nextTick vs Promise
snippet.explanation: Node runs nextTick callbacks before other microtasks — know this when debugging server ordering.

snippet.label: No microtask queue in C#
snippet.explanation: C# does not serialize all continuations on one thread unless SynchronizationContext forces it — unlike JS microtasks on one agent thread.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Assuming setTimeout(fn, 0) runs before Promise.then. Creating infinite microtask chains that starve rendering and I/O. Forgetting Node nextTick priority.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: log with performance.now() and labels in staging when race bugs appear after await. In Chrome DevTools, enable 'Async' call stack on breakpoints to see microtask continuations. If macrotasks never run, search for recursive queueMicrotask without await.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Minimum delay not zero in practice

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot predict A/B/promise/timeout ordering. Claiming C# Task uses a microtask queue. Saying async/await is multi-threaded.

interviewTakeaways: Microtasks drain completely before the next macrotask; Promise.then is a microtask.
async/await continuations are microtasks — ordering follows Promise rules.
Node process.nextTick runs before Promise microtasks.
60s: Sync first. All microtasks. One macrotask. Repeat. setTimeout 0 is not immediate. await resumes as microtask.
